strategyPosture: Hold the risk-tolerant posture the data grants — credit is calm, the rebuilt momentum gate reads FULL at 100% exposure — but keep new exposure staged and probed into the DATA_AHEAD dislocation cluster, nothing full-size. The arb board's single TRADEABLE (WBD, 14.8% annualized into the Oct 6 close) is a 4-day binary, not a position.

themes.counterRead: The relief trade is honest about its limits: nobody is pricing a Fed pivot, only a pause. That matches the data — a cool print against hot activity (ADP +90k, Chicago PMI 58.8) is genuinely ambiguous, and the tape is treating it that way. The risk is not mispricing today but complacency if CPI on Oct 14 runs hot against this calm.
themes.dataAnchor: August PCE printed 3.4% headline (vs 3.7% expected) and 3.0% core (vs 3.3%), cutting October hike odds from ~70% to ~35-47%. But the 10-year closed at 5.29% and the 30-year at 5.64% — both multi-decade highs — and the early rally faded: Nasdaq +0.25%, S&P -0.3%, Dow -0.9% on Sep 30. Small caps never participated: IWM is -5.25% over one month and -6.85% over three.
themes.label: Cool print, hot tape underneath
themes.narrative: PCE came in cool, hike odds collapsed, and the market breathed out — the inflation scare is over and the path is clear.
themes.watchFor: October CPI (Oct 14): a hot print against current calm reprices the pause fast.

themes.counterRead: This is the same distribution-not-crisis read the radar has carried all week, and the concentration data keeps confirming it. The one thing to respect: the divergence gap itself (-9.23) is real, and credit can flip faster than equity positioning. SLOOS at 0% is permission, not a guarantee.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages -11.33% from 52-week highs vs SPY at -2.1% — a -9.23 point divergence gap — while bank lending standards sit at 0% (SLOOS, deep in LOOSE territory, far from the ~40% stress threshold). NVDA is the strongest megacap at -3.4% from highs; TSLA the weakest at -28.9%.
themes.label: Index calm masks concentrated damage
themes.narrative: The S&P is only 2% off its highs — the market looks healthy.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.0 or SLOOS jumping toward 20% — either revokes the rotation thesis.

themes.counterRead: The washout is indiscriminate: names with 20-55% revenue growth and strong FCF trade 30-60% below highs on sentiment, not on broken numbers. That is the textbook DATA_AHEAD setup — but 'cheap' has been early all year, so this is staged-probe territory, not a blanket bid. The momentum engine's rebuilt gate reads stress 0/3 (FULL, 100% exposure), which grants permission without forcing size.
themes.dataAnchor: 25 tracked dislocations, led by software (HUBS -59.2% from highs, APP -60.6%, NOW -30.6%, MDB -26.3% on an acute catalyst) and the nuclear/power complex (BWXT -43.3%, VST -36.3% with $1.17M insider buying at the trough, NXT -52.2%). Revenues are growing 16-55% YoY across the cluster with FCF margins intact. Semis equipment is already turning: AMAT +11.6% and LRCX +9.0% over one month with RSI near 60.
themes.label: Software and nuclear washouts vs intact fundamentals
themes.narrative: These sectors are broken — the selling must know something.
themes.watchFor: AVGO (-29.1%, revenue +23.9%, 67.8% gross margin) stabilizing — it is the highest-conviction name in the cluster at score 81.

themes.counterRead: The sprint has the shape of late-cycle concentration: one name doing the work of ten. META's 27% month against a -1.53% day smells like chasing, and crypto's bounce (BTC +9.47%, ETH +10.53% over one month) rides the same risk bid. Trim-into-strength remains the posture, not fresh exposure.
themes.dataAnchor: META is +27.1% over one month — the single strongest 1-month move in the tracked universe — while the next tier (RKLB +14.35%) is a different asset class entirely. Crypto bounced with the relief trade but faded with it (BTC gave back gains post-print). Uranium, the prior sprint complex, washed out -11% to -14% over the same month (CCJ, URA, SMR).
themes.label: META/crypto sprint runs ahead of the tape
themes.narrative: META and crypto are leading the next leg — momentum is back.
themes.watchFor: META losing its 1-month trendline — the sprint complex unwinds fast when the leader turns.

watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.0 — revokes the macro permission slip
SPX losing the 200-day — flips the momentum gate to REDUCED/DEFENSIVE
October CPI (Oct 14) — the next inflation verdict after PCE's ambiguity
WBD Oct 6 close — the arb board's sole tradeable resolves or slips
FOMC Oct 27-28 hike odds — currently ~35-47%, the market's central bet
whereWaveBuilds: The next directional move likely comes from the October CPI/FOMC sequence repricing the 'pause' — if inflation re-accelerates against 5.29% tens, the relief trade reverses into the small-cap and duration weak spots first.
